variant_reviews.comparison: The coefficient is sqrt(mu_j) U_j against the H_K-orthonormal phi_j, yielding S_infinity(a)=sum_j sqrt(mu_j) inner(phi_j,a)_K U_j. Nonnegative summable covariance eigenvalues and iid standard normals are needed to prove square summability almost surely; HilbertBasis.hasSum_repr_symm applies once that l2 coefficient element is supplied, and the real Riesz isometry gives a bounded functional. Its theorem is deterministic and does not by itself establish the probability-one event, measurable choice on the complement or centered Gaussian law. Do not change sqrt(mu_j) to mu_j or transfer this basis normalization to the applied R_infinity series.
